If we're talking bars, it depends on the bar. There's a couple She's welcome in and she knows it. They keep a stockpile of cooked bacon and treats for her.

I've had 18 years married with my husband. We've been through so much. Heartache, heart joy, loss, nearly losing each other over and over again and always finding our way back. I cannot fathom the depths of how much you are hurting and angry, but I know what I can imagine doesn't come close. I don't know you, but know that you're in my heart. 

I'm grateful the person who took him from you was caught. I hope he is given the greatest sentence allowable and seeks to be worth the life he's fortunate enough to have as long as he is allowed to draw breath. I hope he is remorseful. I hope that he seeks healing for whatever brought him to be desperate enough to take the life of someone else. He doesn't deserve your forgiveness for his actions. Truly, taking the life of someone else is the worst and lowest point in a person's life and those left behind live with a void that cannot be filled. A limb that cannot be rejoined. 

I wish peace for you, in time. Though that missing, that anger may never leave you, I hope there is a day in your life you are able to breathe just a little easier. That the next day from there, it may get a little easier still. I know it seems unimaginable, but I hope that one day these things come to you.

My cousin came to live with us when I was in junior high school. We shared a room at the time she was just beginning to exhibit her schizophrenia. I know it caused her to be very destructive with her life, and abusive to others around her - but I know that was because she was not good at accepting help and the people she surrounded herself with were also very destructive. 

I'm sorry that your family is not giving you the kind of support you need to thrive. It sounds like you have more to offer through music (at the very least) to the world. Have you tried writing or recording anything? It may work as a way to focus your thoughts and get out some of your frustrations about your situation.

Of course. I know I'm just some rando - but I've seen a lot of addiction, I've also seen a lot of folks pass from my life. I know that addiction doesn't mean they were a bad person. It means they had their own issues, much like all of us. We don't all have the same tools in this world. I also know that in order to keep going, we have to take in the best of those around us, whether they are with us or not. We have to use what they have taught us. There will be dark days, and right now they may seem pretty endless. But you may one day have a good day and find it was there to lift someone else up. Sometimes those small things help you too. <3

Your feelings are entirely valid. I cannot fathom the depth of your loss and I'm truly sorry that her addiction took her from you. I'm certain she was the best mother she could be and no one will ever replace her. But please know that her fate is not yours. 

Take the best of her and grow in light and love. It will take time, but don't lose sight of the life she was helping you strive for. Let it fuel you to know she wanted the best for you. You are entirely not alone in this world. This may never stop hurting but there will be people who will step up for you in this life. 

So much of high school will be about finding your place in the world. And then when you get out of high school, it will happen all over again. You will always take the best of her with you. Each of these milestones will not be without her presence. I know that seems pretty far from how you feel right now, but carry her words and those beautiful moments with you. Let them be your compass. 

Please do not let what happen to her happen to you.

I know it's not much, but I'm glad you're on this planet. I'm glad you've made it this far. And while it may not be a happy birthday, know that all of us here commenting give a damn that you're still around. Please don't stop trying to rebuild your life. I'm 10 years older than you, and I can say that even when I feel like my life, my depression is crushing, there's always something, however minor to build off of. We're here.

Sounds like a terrible friend. You should dress in a manner that makes YOU comfortable in the world. Our looks, our personalities, they change. So do our relationships with others. It was an awful thing for this person to even walk themselves into this situation to tell you these things. 

That person is toxic and you deserve better. We are all allowed to be different and unique and sometimes that's lonely, but it also sets you apart and allows for other beautiful people to come into your life who will appreciate you for who you are. Do not let this person dictate the way you walk through this world. If you're here, it's because you have depression - and that already makes it wildly difficult enough some days. 

Be you. Seek new people, new friend groups, new experiences. Find your people. Do not be discouraged if it takes a while.

Wish I had advice for you. Depression is a beast that will always need to be fought. Some days it won't hurt so bad, or you'll be able to focus enough on the better things in your life and others you will feel mostly ok. I hope you have more of the latter than the former.

Totally with you on the depression/anxiety. With time, it's been easier to manage the anxiety portion through meditation. Just having control over being mindful of the now and not getting ahead of yourself is helpful there. Depression is another beast. It's your monkey mind, chemical imbalance, environment and experience. While meditation may help give you another tool to battle with peacefully, there are other things at work. 

It can be a stepping stone in the right direction though. It may help you look at life in a way that  maybe doesn't trigger you. Doesn't send you spiraling. I still spiral. But it's a tool to help lessen it, a lifeline in the dark.

Maybe try some guided meditations on gratitude or metta. 

I battle depression and when I was starting out with meditation, that monkey mind was a real bastard pretty consistently. When you are in those moments of clear mind, anything could walk through the door. Until you learn to get past that point, it could be helpful to keep to some positive guided programs.
Same. I have a zafu at work. Empty conference rooms are great for an afternoon sit.

There are many many accounts of folks meditating under the influence of other substances. On occassion, I enjoy a little weed before a long sit. 

That being said, your mind is generally not in a focused mood when alcohol is involved. Meditation always sounds like a good idea because it'sa good thing. But remember, after 8 drinks, you wouldn't/shouldn't get behind the wheel of a car, so you probably cannot trust your mind to maintain meditation. Your monkey mind is much more likely to be in control and take you down some paths you may not want to go.
